purpose: Mifepristone is used for two main purposes. In combination with another medicine called misoprostol, it is used to end an early pregnancy (up to 10 weeks). It is also used to control high blood sugar in adults with a condition called Cushing's syndrome who also have type 2 diabetes.
how_it_works: Your body uses a hormone called progesterone to support a pregnancy. Mifepristone blocks the effects of progesterone, which stops the pregnancy from continuing. In Cushing's syndrome, it works by blocking the effects of cortisol, a stress hormone that is too high and is causing problems like high blood sugar.
common_side_effects: Cramping and abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding or spotting, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, and feeling tired. When used for Cushing's syndrome, it may also cause low potassium levels, swelling, and fatigue.
warnings: If used for ending a pregnancy, you must follow up with your doctor to make sure the process is complete — incomplete treatment can be serious. Do not use it if you have certain bleeding disorders, are on blood thinners, or have an IUD in place. Rarely, serious infections can occur — seek care immediately if you have fever, severe pain, or heavy bleeding. For Cushing's syndrome use, it can cause serious drops in potassium and affect adrenal gland function. This medicine is only available through certified healthcare providers.
typical_dosing: For ending a pregnancy: typically one 200 mg tablet taken by mouth on day one, followed by misoprostol 24 to 48 hours later, as directed by your doctor. For Cushing's syndrome: usually starts at 300 mg once daily with a meal, and your doctor may slowly increase the dose based on how you respond, up to a maximum of 1200 mg per day.
